The Nigeria Customs Service on Tuesday unveiled the first episode of its new original television drama series, Novara. Speaking during the premiere in Apapa, the National Public Relations Officer of the Service, Abdullahi Maiwada, explained that the series was part of efforts to promote public understanding of its operations, highlight the sacrifices of its officers and strengthen public engagement through creative storytelling. Maiwada said the 79-episode series, which explores the human experiences behind Customs operations, is scheduled to premiere on Africa Magic Showcase early January 2027. He said the initiative marked a significant milestone in the Service’s communication strategy, taking its institutional messaging beyond conventional channels to the entertainment industry. “Novara is designed to educate, inform and entertain audiences while promoting the values of integrity, courage, professionalism, patriotism, resilience and responsible service to the nation,” Maiwada said. He explained that although the Service’s statutory responsibilities revolve around revenue generation, trade facilitation and border security, the personal sacrifices and challenges faced by officers in carrying out these duties are often not adequately understood by the public. The NCS image-maker said that officers operate in challenging environments, confront sophisticated transnational criminal networks and sometimes put their lives at risk to protect the country’s economic interests and territorial integrity. “The series, therefore, seeks to bring these experiences to the screen by portraying officers not only as law enforcement personnel but also as parents, spouses and members of society whose professional responsibilities often affect their family lives.” Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources He disclosed that the television series would run for 79 episodes, adding that the first season, comprising 39 episodes, had been completed and was ready for broadcast, while production of the remaining 40 episodes was ongoing. Maiwada said that after its premiere on 7 January 2027, the series would air twice weekly, every Tuesday and Friday at 9pm, on Africa Magic Showcase. Responding to questions about the production’s financing, Maiwada revealed that Novara was being produced under a public–private partnership arrangement, noting that the NCS’s support was largely in kind rather than through direct financial contributions. He said the service provided institutional assistance, including access to relevant locations and operational facilities, personnel, costumes, uniforms, props and supporting cast members selected from its workforce. Native Media also contributed camera and other technical production equipment,” the NCS spokesman stated. He said that the funding arrangement demonstrated how public institutions could leverage private-sector partnerships to deliver impactful communication initiatives without placing the entire production budget on public resources. Novara is the story of Pancha; a Customs officer caught between his family responsibilities and his professional commitment to protecting Nigeria against economic sabotage and transnational organised crime. The series tells the story of the dangerous world of an organised criminal cartel involved in smuggling illicit drugs and arms into Nigeria. The syndicate, led by a notorious drug lord identified as Jambala, reportedly operates in collaboration with a Mexican drug network with links to the United States. As the criminal network expands its operations, Pancha and his team in the Customs Intelligence Unit embark on a high-risk undercover mission to expose and dismantle the syndicate. The assignment, however, places his family in danger and tests his determination to remain committed to national service. He explained that the series explores the challenges of balancing professional obligations with family responsibilities, while highlighting the threats posed by drug trafficking, arms smuggling and other forms of transnational organised crime. The storyline also underscores the significance of intelligence-driven operations, collaboration among security agencies and institutional vigilance in tackling security challenges. The production features a team of professionals from Nigeria’s film and television industry, with Agbode Ugo and Roger Oppen as producers. Shot in Lagos, Nigeria, and Los Angeles, United States, the series blends indigenous storytelling with an international production perspective to capture the cross-border dimensions of certain security and economic crimes. The first season stars Topher Olowuya, Ray Adeka, Sharon Owojimi, Charles Okwong, Similayo Hassan and Iwande Osioma, among others, and is directed by Daniel Oranyi and Ben Cheadika.
